independence_caveat: Same model family as the other reviewers; agreement is reading consistency, not independent validation.

findings.finding: C11 is correctly scoped rather than a reproduction claim: the manuscript explicitly says no new fit, no axis selection, and no independent validation, and that cited numerical results come from source packages. Prior numbers therefore remain inherited unless the cited package replay is separately demonstrated.
findings.test: Re-run every inherited numerical result from the cited package version, input data, command/configuration, and recorded output hash; absent those, retain an un-reproduced status.
findings.reasoning: The limitation is stated explicitly and no execution evidence is offered. The manuscript does not claim that the prior numerical chain was regenerated here.

findings.finding: C12 is internally consistent within the frozen manuscript: it marks byte-for-byte PDF reproducibility as open because of timestamp/trailer bytes, while separately reporting a current warning-free build. A single clean build is not the same property as byte identity, so the sentence itself does not claim achieved bitwise reproducibility.
findings.test: Build the unchanged source twice and compare SHA-256 values, PDF creation/modification metadata, and trailer identifiers.
findings.reasoning: The manuscript distinguishes build completion and warning status from byte-for-byte reproducibility and explicitly labels the latter an open workflow item.

findings.finding: The open-item caveat is technically supported, but the referenced implementation does not close it: the build-script comment says the output is deterministic given the .tex, while the TeX source has no SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH or PDF metadata/trailer-ID suppression. The recipe starts from mutable texlive:latest-minimal, the script checks only the mutable efc-tex:2026 tag, and no image digest or complete source-tree hash is recorded.
findings.test: Pin the container by immutable image digest and the source tree by manifest hash, suppress or normalize PDF timestamps and trailer IDs, run the exact script twice, and compare complete PDF bytes and checksums.
findings.reasoning: The existing PDF exposes a creation timestamp and trailer ID, and the source contains no controls for suppressing them. The script's deterministic comment conflicts with a byte-level reading of C12 and the mutable toolchain cannot establish a reproducible environment.

findings.finding: The statement that the current build has no Overfull/Underfull hbox or float-placement warnings is not independently evidenced by the supplied reproducibility chain. Both pdflatex passes redirect stdout to /dev/null, the script does not parse log files for those warnings, and the package contains neither a build log nor .build.sha256. The existing PDF hash proves one artifact exists, not that the run was warning-free.
findings.source: snapshot.tex line 346; efc_pdf_bygg.sh lines 46-56; current package inventory
findings.test: Run the two passes while retaining their logs, fail on explicit Overfull/Underfull/float-warning patterns, and persist the exact source, container digest, logs, and resulting .build.sha256.
findings.reasoning: A PDF is present (sha256 1a00690b21d67e30c9f0e8fd64db0867902a54d9968c847dc3c135ff447d067a), but no warning capture or checksum sidecar is present in the package.

findings.finding: The full AI-friendly stack named in the reproducibility section is not present in the current package. The frozen TeX says the directory is designed to carry src/, data/, and examples/ after text freeze, but the EFC_Model_Family_Reconciliation directory has no such directories; ai_manifest.json lists only 11 top-level files, and index.json/metadata.json expose only PDF and README as package files. The wording is prospective (designed), but the achieved package cannot regenerate code/data/examples, and its manifest is stale: it records TeX/PDF sizes of 24741/317321 bytes versus actual 32245/343090 bytes.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 344-346 compared with the current package manifests and directory inventory
findings.test: Require src/, data/, and examples/ in the package validator; regenerate the manifest after text freeze; record exact per-file hashes and verify the manifest against the directory before release.
findings.reasoning: The snapshot TeX and the package TeX have the same SHA-256 (99e69c41944a71c738a3d3fa9f4366d41fb51a17060e7a5e0c5cafa246150ee1), so this is the same frozen text. The current directory has no promised executable or data subtrees and its recorded byte sizes do not match the files on disk.

findings.finding: C8's open provenance diagnosis is reproducibility-consistent: the manuscript reports null Delta-chi-squared/significance and no new fit performed, so the >=5-sigma exclusion cannot be regenerated from this frozen work. No SPARC data snapshot, fit code/configuration, source-package version, or output checksum is supplied. This supports keeping the exclusion open rather than treating it as a reproduced result.
findings.test: Supply the source DOI/version, data release, fit script and configuration, exact inputs and outputs, and checksums; rerun and populate Delta-chi-squared and significance fields.
findings.reasoning: The text itself identifies the missing execution and provenance fields. A reproduction verdict stronger than open would contradict the stated null metadata.

findings.finding: C9 is not yet a determinate replay specification: three a0 candidates circulate, the author freeze is absent, and no SPARC dataset/version, command/configuration, or input/output hash is supplied. The manuscript correctly labels the discriminator proposed and not executed, so this is a regeneration boundary, not a failed run.
findings.test: Author-freeze exactly one a0 value and its origin, pin the SPARC data release and preprocessing, publish the command/configuration and hashes, then execute the retrodiction without fitting a0.
findings.reasoning: The missing freeze and absent execution artifacts are explicit in the manuscript; the proposed status is therefore honest but not reproducible yet.

findings.finding: C10 likewise has no determinate replay: alpha, phi0, phi(z), and the field normalization are not frozen, and no standard-siren data release, likelihood code/configuration, or output hash is supplied. The manuscript explicitly calls the discriminator proposed and not executed, so no achieved reproducibility should be inferred.
findings.test: Freeze alpha, phi0, phi(z), and field normalization; pin the standard-siren data release and likelihood implementation; publish configuration and hashes; then rerun the comparison.
findings.reasoning: The text discloses the unfrozen parameters and the absence of execution. That is compatible with a proposal, but it is insufficient for regeneration.

findings.finding: C14 is reproducibly enumerated only at identifier/scope level: Table 1 names six exact package slugs and DOIs, while the text separately names broader corpus packages and rejects an exclusive six-package set. However, no exact package versions, repository commit IDs, or per-file checksums are frozen, so the scope statement alone cannot regenerate the code/data measurement chain.
findings.test: Resolve every listed persistent identifier, record the exact version and repository commit, create per-file manifests, and verify the package set before replaying any result.
findings.reasoning: The manuscript supplies a useful package inventory and explicitly states its non-closed scope, but DOI-level identity does not fix the bytes, code revision, or data inputs needed for regeneration.
